issues.legal_issue: A landlord who is not in actual possession may apply to review an allotment or release order, and the review deadline applicable to a person in lawful occupation does not bar the landlord.
material_facts: The premises had five co-owners, and the applicant for review was a landlord who was not in occupation of the premises when the allotment order was made.
A tenant received an allotment order and took possession of the premises.
The non-occupant landlord applied to review the allotment order 25 days after it was made.
issues.conclusion: A landlord may apply to review an allotment or release order even if not in actual possession; the seven-day proviso does not restrict that right.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 16(5)(a) of the U.P. Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972, “the landlord or any other person” identifies separate categories, and the lawful-occupation requirement applies only to the latter. The seven-day proviso applies to a person in lawful occupation and does not curtail a landlord’s substantive right. A proviso ordinarily does not take away substantive rights unless that intention is clear. The Court approved Niren Kumar Das v. The District Judge, Pilibhit, AIR 1977 Allahabad 47.

rule.if: review_of_allotment_or_release_order and applicant_is_landlord and landlord_not_in_actual_occupation and application_filed_after_short_deadline

predicates.review_of_allotment_or_release_order: A person applied to review an order allotting or releasing a building.
predicates.applicant_is_landlord: The person who applied for review was a landlord of the building.
predicates.landlord_not_in_actual_occupation: The landlord was not in actual occupation of the building when the order was made.
predicates.application_filed_after_short_deadline: The landlord filed the review application after the short deadline applicable to a person in lawful occupation.
predicates.landlord_may_seek_review: A landlord may seek review of the allotment or release order despite not being in actual occupation or filing after the short deadline.

issues.definition: When a landlord seeks review of an allotment or release order, the landlord may seek review even if not in actual occupation and the application was filed after the short deadline.
